claims.text: Lumbar plexus: arises from all the lumbar spinal nerves and supplies the pelvic region and anterior leg.
claims.quote: The lumbar plexus arises from all the lumbar spinal nerves and gives rise to nerves innervating the pelvic region and the anterior leg.

claims.text: Femoral nerve: a major lumbar plexus nerve; its saphenous branch extends through the anterior lower leg.
claims.quote: The femoral nerve is one of the major nerves from this plexus, which gives rise to the saphenous nerve as a branch that extends through the anterior lower leg.

claims.text: Sacral plexus: from L4 and L5 and S1 to S4.
claims.quote: The sacral plexus comes from the lower lumbar nerves L4 and L5 and the sacral nerves S1 to S4.

claims.text: Sciatic nerve: the main sacral plexus nerve, combining the tibial and fibular nerves; compression or irritation of it or its roots causes sciatica.
claims.quote: The most significant systemic nerve to come from this plexus is the sciatic nerve, which is a combination of the tibial nerve and the fibular nerve. The sciatic nerve extends across the hip joint and is most commonly associated with the condition sciatica, which is the result of compression or irritation of the nerve or any of the spinal nerves giving rise to it.

claims.text: Peroneal (fibular) nerve palsy: usually compression of the nerve against the lateral fibular neck.
claims.quote: Peroneal nerve palsy is usually caused by compression of the nerve against the lateral aspect of the fibular neck.

claims.text: Footdrop: weak dorsiflexion and eversion, sometimes with sensory loss over the anterolateral lower leg and dorsum of the foot or the first web space.
claims.quote: Peroneal nerve palsy causes footdrop (weakened dorsiflexion and eversion of the foot) and, occasionally, a sensory deficit in the anterolateral aspect of the lower leg and the dorsum of the foot or in the web space between the first and second metatarsals.

claims.text: Peroneal vs L5: L5 radiculopathy can look the same but tends to also weaken hip abduction by the gluteus medius.
claims.quote: L5 radiculopathy can cause similar deficits but, unlike peroneal nerve palsy, tends to weaken hip abduction by the gluteus medius.

claims.text: Plexus pattern: lumbar plexus lesions affect the legs; sacral plexus lesions affect the pelvis and legs.
claims.quote: Lumbar plexus: Legs Sacral plexus: Pelvis and legs

claims.text: Anticoagulation: a hematoma may compress the lumbosacral plexus.
claims.quote: In patients receiving anticoagulants, a hematoma may compress the lumbosacral plexus.
